items.question: If Dark Magician of Chaos gets Special Summoned partway through a chain and isn't the last thing to resolve, do I still get a Spell Card back from my Graveyard?

expected.answer: No. If Dark Magician of Chaos is Special Summoned in the middle of a chain, its optional trigger effect misses the timing, so you do not return a Spell Card from your Graveyard to your hand.

items.answer:
No — you do not get a Spell Card back in that case.

"Dark Magician of Chaos"'s Spell retrieval is an optional Trigger Effect with a "when ... successfully" condition, so it has to be the last thing to resolve for the timing to be correct. The ruling on the card says exactly this: if it is Special Summoned in the middle of a chain (not the last effect in the chain to resolve), the timing is not correct and you do **not** return a Spell Card from your Graveyard to your hand.

Note that this is about *mid-chain* Summons, not about cards like "Monster Gate" or "Reasoning": when "Dark Magician of Chaos" is Special Summoned by "Monster Gate", its effect still activates, but only after "Monster Gate" has fully resolved — so you can even retrieve a Spell Card that "Monster Gate" itself sent to the Graveyard. The difference is that "Monster Gate" finishes resolving entirely, leaving "Dark Magician of Chaos"'s Summon as the last thing that happened.

Sources:
- [Dark Magician of Chaos ruling — Missing the Timing](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/dark-magician-of-chaos#ruling-48b36240-1344-444b-9155-3d4b76cef93a): if Special Summoned mid-chain, the Optional Trigger Effect misses its timing and you do not retrieve a Spell Card.
- [Monster Gate ruling naming Dark Magician of Chaos](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/monster-gate#ruling-dec56e07-a726-41aa-89d2-66bfd6c4884f): the effect activates after "Monster Gate" has fully resolved, so Spell Cards sent to the Graveyard by "Monster Gate" can be retrieved.
- [Dark Magician of Chaos ruling — Reasoning](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/dark-magician-of-chaos#ruling-c79cfc84-f38c-492b-8a22-04f60aa4f005): its effect activates when Special Summoned by "Reasoning" (the Summon is the last thing to resolve).

items.question: If I discard Night Assailant to pay for Tribe-Infecting Virus, does Night Assailant's effect go off?

expected.answer: Yes. Night Assailant only has to be sent to the Graveyard, so discarding it as a cost for Tribe-Infecting Virus or Magic Jammer activates its effect, after the current chain resolves.

items.answer:
I'll look up both cards first. **Yes — Night Assailant's second effect activates, but only after the whole chain containing Tribe-Infecting Virus's effect resolves.**

The ruling on Night Assailant is explicit: its effect "activates when sent to the Graveyard as a cost for 'Magic Jammer' or 'Tribe-Infecting Virus'; 'Night Assailant''s effect activates after the current chain resolves." It doesn't matter that the discard was a cost rather than an effect. The End of Anubis ruling shows the same timing — when Night Assailant is discarded for Tribe-Infecting Virus and Fiend is named, Night Assailant's effect is activated after Tribe-Infecting Virus resolves.

Two things to keep in mind:
- Night Assailant cannot select itself (so no loop), so you need a *different* Flip Effect Monster in your Graveyard to return. If the only Flip Effect Monster in the Graveyard is the Night Assailant you just discarded, there is nothing to get back.
- This is unlike a "when… you can" card such as Peten the Dark Clown, whose effect does *not* activate when discarded as a cost for Tribe-Infecting Virus; Night Assailant's is a plain "when sent" trigger with no missed-timing restriction stated.

Also note the effect is negated entirely while The End of Anubis is face-up on the field — but in the Tribe-Infecting Virus scenario where Fiend is named, Anubis is destroyed first, which is why Night Assailant's effect still goes off afterwards.

Sources:
- [Night Assailant ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/night-assailant#ruling-e76248d6-36e1-414d-914f-0fdac0e7a08c) — effect activates when sent as a cost for Tribe-Infecting Virus, after the current chain resolves.
- [Night Assailant ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/night-assailant#ruling-dc6bffa4-e053-407d-a298-6cdd1c90c679) — it cannot select itself, so no infinite loop.
- [The End of Anubis ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/the-end-of-anubis#ruling-e043553d-5e50-4299-aa87-9c866fbe9dc5) — Night Assailant discarded for Tribe-Infecting Virus activates after it resolves.
- [The End of Anubis ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/the-end-of-anubis#ruling-8082d010-bc79-42cd-b9db-cc9d00c47df7) — Anubis negates Night Assailant's second effect while on the field.
- [Peten the Dark Clown ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/peten-the-dark-clown#ruling-30e34349-6eba-4c01-b54b-8d5af869fbee) — contrast: that card's "when… you can" effect does not activate when discarded for Tribe-Infecting Virus.

items.question: My opponent used Nobleman of Crossout on my face-down Sangan. Do I get to search with Sangan?

expected.answer: No. Nobleman of Crossout removes the monster from play so it never goes to the Graveyard, and Sangan's effect does not activate.

items.answer:
No — you do not get to search with "Sangan."

"Nobleman of Crossout" destroys the face-down monster and removes it from play, so "Sangan" never goes to the Graveyard, and its effect (which triggers only when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard) does not activate. The ruling under Nobleman of Crossout says this explicitly: the targeted monster is removed from play and never goes to the Graveyard, "so the effects of cards like 'Sangan' will not activate." The related ruling also confirms that a face-down Flip Effect Monster hit by Nobleman of Crossout is not flipped face-up and its Flip Effect is not activated (Sangan is not a Flip Effect Monster anyway, and no copies would be removed from the Decks here).

- [Nobleman of Crossout ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/nobleman-of-crossout#ruling-b82f1a2a-1721-4342-a98c-bfe1f7eff4eb) — the monster is removed from play and never goes to the Graveyard, so "Sangan"'s effect will not activate.

items.question: When Mystic Tomato dies in battle and pulls out another monster, can I respond with Torrential Tribute?

expected.answer: No. Torrential Tribute cannot be activated during the Damage Step, so it cannot be used against monsters Special Summoned by Mystic Tomato and similar cards that summon when destroyed by battle.

items.answer:
I'll look up both cards first. **No.** You cannot activate Torrential Tribute against the monster Special Summoned by Mystic Tomato.

Mystic Tomato's effect activates when it is sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle, so the Special Summon happens during the Damage Step. Torrential Tribute's own ruling states plainly that it **cannot be activated during the Damage Step**, and that this specifically bars it from being used against monsters Special Summoned by "Mystic Tomato," "Giant Rat," "Nimble Momonga," "Masked Dragon" and similar cards — as well as against "Cyber Jar" or "Morphing Jar #2" flipped face-up by an attack. Mystic Tomato's page says the same thing: "Since the Special Summoning occurs during the Damage Step, 'Torrential Tribute', etc. cannot be used." The Damage Step guide section adds that only the effects of monsters and Counter Traps can be used to negate things there — Normal Traps cannot.

Note that this is about timing, not about Torrential Tribute being unable to respond to a Special Summon in general — it can be activated after a monster is Summoned through another card's effect such as "Monster Reborn" or "Call of the Haunted." It is simply locked out during the Damage Step.

Sources:
- [Mystic Tomato ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/mystic-tomato#ruling-1f1cb147-79d9-4134-a9a3-b1304b88273b) — because the Special Summon happens in the Damage Step, "Torrential Tribute" cannot be used.
- [Torrential Tribute ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/torrential-tribute#ruling-10da53bf-8455-4974-b8a4-ef37247941ed) — Torrential Tribute cannot be activated during the Damage Step, expressly including against "Mystic Tomato."
- [Torrential Tribute ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/torrential-tribute#ruling-126ff640-f16b-4b96-9a41-a4a31d0875c3) — it can be activated after Summons through card effects like "Monster Reborn."
- [Rulings: The Damage Step](https://beta.goatformat.com/learn/rulings#the-damage-step) — only monster effects and Counter Traps can negate in the Damage Step; Normal Traps cannot be used.

items.question: My opponent activated a Spell Card. Can I chain Breaker the Magical Warrior's effect to it to destroy something?

expected.answer: No. Breaker the Magical Warrior's effect is Spell Speed 1, so you cannot chain it to the activation of a Spell Card.

items.answer:
I'll look up Breaker the Magical Warrior first.

 

 **No.** Breaker the Magical Warrior's counter-removal effect is Spell Speed 1, so it cannot be chained to the activation of a Spell Card (or to any other effect).

Breaker's destruction effect is a cost-paying Spell Speed 1 effect: you remove the Spell Counter as a cost, and the ruling states plainly that because it is Spell Speed 1 you cannot chain it to the activation of a Spell Card. A separate Netrep ruling says the same — the removal is a Cost Effect, Speed 1, and "may not be chained to any other effect." Note also that you cannot activate it at all if there are no Spell or Trap Cards on the field to destroy.

Two related points that come up alongside this:
- The Spell Counter placement when Breaker is Normal Summoned is itself a chain, and it is Spell Speed 1 as well — the counter is placed by the effect, not instantly, so "Trap Hole" / "Ring of Destruction" chained to that placement resolve first (and the counter is not yet on him).
- Removing the counter is a cost, so once you have activated the effect and paid it, the destruction still applies even if Breaker is destroyed in a chain (e.g. by "Ring of Destruction", which will deal 1600 damage to each player).

**Sources**
- [Breaker the Magical Warrior ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/breaker-the-magical-warrior#ruling-4be562d8-66e2-4cd3-9f91-904d24fd047d) — his effect is Spell Speed 1, so it cannot be chained to a Spell Card's activation.
- [Breaker the Magical Warrior ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/breaker-the-magical-warrior#ruling-622f2bfa-bd6b-4582-aaeb-80d194ca6c6a) — counter removal is a Speed 1 Cost Effect, not chainable to any other effect.
- [Breaker the Magical Warrior ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/breaker-the-magical-warrior#ruling-ff757e91-0b29-446a-b3f8-909e1ee56894) — effect cannot be activated with no Spell/Trap Cards on the field.
- [Breaker the Magical Warrior ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/breaker-the-magical-warrior#ruling-4af3148e-14ed-48e5-b052-4cca5e1bacf9) — placing the counter is a chain after the Summon; chained Trap Hole/Ring resolves first.
- [Breaker the Magical Warrior ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/breaker-the-magical-warrior#ruling-812a2aff-a31a-4da7-a604-cd56bc707ecb) — removing the counter is a cost; the destruction still applies if he is destroyed in response.

items.question: I'm attacking and my opponent flips Mirror Force. If I chain Book of Moon to flip my attacker face-down, does it survive?

items.answer:
Yes. If you chain **Book of Moon** to **Mirror Force** and flip your attacking monster face-down, that monster is not destroyed by **Mirror Force**.

**Book of Moon** resolves first and flips the attacker into face-down Defense Position. Then **Mirror Force** resolves, but it only destroys Attack Position monsters, so the flipped monster is spared. items.question: My opponent's Fiber Jar flipped up and its effect activated. Can I stop it by chaining Book of Moon to turn it back face-down?

expected.answer: No. Book of Moon flips the monster face-down again, but the Flip Effect of a monster like Fiber Jar still resolves as normal.

items.answer:
I'll look up both cards first. **No.** Chaining "Book of Moon" to flip "Fiber Jar" back face-down does not stop its Flip Effect — the effect still resolves as normal.

The rulings are explicit on this point. One ruling under "Book of Moon" gives "Fiber Jar" as its example: if you chain "Book of Moon" to the activation of a Flip Effect Monster's effect, "Book of Moon" flips the monster face-down again, but the Flip Effect still resolves as normal. A related ruling states the general principle: when "Book of Moon" is chained to a Flip effect, the Flip effect resolves as normally unless the Flip effect requires the monster to remain face-up — and "Fiber Jar" does not. "Fiber Jar"'s effect shuffles all cards on the field, in hands, and in Graveyards into the Decks, including "Fiber Jar" itself, and it even applies when "Fiber Jar" has been attacked and destroyed by battle, so it clearly doesn't care whether "Fiber Jar" is still face-up when it resolves.

One practical note: "Fiber Jar" is Forbidden in this format, so this situation shouldn't come up in a legal Goat Format game.

items.question: If my opponent responds to my Call of the Haunted by destroying it with Mystical Space Typhoon, do I still get my monster?

expected.answer: No. If Call of the Haunted is destroyed in a chain to its own activation, the monster it would Special Summon is not Special Summoned.

items.answer:
I'll look up both cards first. No — if Mystical Space Typhoon is chained to your Call of the Haunted, Call of the Haunted is destroyed before it ever Special Summons anything, and its effect disappears.

**Why:** Call of the Haunted is a Continuous Trap Card, so it must still be on the field when its effect resolves. Mystical Space Typhoon (chain link 2) resolves first and destroys it, so when Call of the Haunted would resolve there is nothing there to Summon the monster.

**Watch the order, though:** if it's the other way around — Mystical Space Typhoon already activated and targeting Call of the Haunted, and you chain Call of the Haunted to it — then Call of the Haunted resolves first and you *do* get your monster. But Mystical Space Typhoon then resolves and destroys Call of the Haunted, which in turn destroys that monster. So you only keep the monster if Call of the Haunted survives, e.g. its destruction is prevented or its effect is negated, or the monster is protected (a monster equipped with Heart of Clear Water, for instance, is not destroyed when Call of the Haunted is destroyed).

Sources:
- [Call of the Haunted ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/call-of-the-haunted#ruling-271f8428-efd9-4a0e-a5d2-4765e7fc1961) — Mystical Space Typhoon chained to Call of the Haunted destroys it before the Summon, and "Call of the Haunted's effect will then disappear"; also covers the reversed order.
- [Mystical Space Typhoon ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/mystical-space-typhoon#ruling-5ca453c3-5c4e-47c8-8416-d65d43ab9110) — same text, filed under Mystical Space Typhoon.

items.question: What happens if Morphing Jar flips up and one of us has only 3 cards left in the Deck?

expected.answer: That player loses the Duel. If either player has fewer than 5 cards in their Deck when Morphing Jar's Flip Effect activates, that player loses because the card says draw.

items.answer:
I'll look up Morphing Jar first. **That player loses the Duel.** Morphing Jar's effect tells both players to draw 5 cards, and the rulings say a player who can't draw the full 5 because their Deck is short loses.

Details from the ruling:
- "If there are fewer than 5 cards in the Deck of either player when this card's Flip Effect is activated, that player will lose the Duel, since the text of this card says 'draw.'" Three cards is fewer than 5, so that player loses.
- The effect still resolves as a whole: both players discard their hands first, "after that" both draw 5. The short-Deck player simply can't complete the draw.
- This is different from pick-up effects: with Cyber Jar, a player with fewer than 5 cards does not lose, because Cyber Jar's text picks up cards rather than drawing them. Morphing Jar says "draw," which is why the loss applies.
- It also differs from milling, like Needle Worm, where the remaining cards just go to the Graveyard and the player only loses later when a draw is actually required.

One timing note, since "after that, draw" and other resolution effects can interact: loss from an incomplete draw happens during resolution, so effects that trigger afterward (for example Magical Thorn's damage, which is dealt after the effect resolves) won't get to apply — there is a ruling where a player with only one card left in the Deck loses to their own Morphing Jar before Magical Thorn damages the opponent.

Sources:
- [Morphing Jar ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/morphing-jar#ruling-82a731ee-7f7d-4415-81e7-e52d803bcda4) — fewer than 5 cards in either Deck means that player loses, because the card says "draw."
- [Morphing Jar card text / read](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/morphing-jar) — both players discard all cards in hand, then both draw 5.
- [Cyber Jar ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/cyber-jar#ruling-71cd16e0-df2e-466e-99ea-388365d21cef) — picking up cards instead of drawing does not cause a loss.
- [Needle Worm ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/needle-worm#ruling-bf70c472-2781-4f53-8822-0399aa15b542) — contrast with milling, where the player does not lose immediately.
- [Magical Thorn ruling](https://beta.goatformat.com/cards/magical-thorn#ruling-ee0080be-0cd3-4577-acb5-628d5f42d482) — the loss from the short Deck happens before post-resolution damage.
